# Let unused links decay and mark dead links

## Intent

A library that only grows becomes the 600 open tabs it was meant to replace. This package lets links the owner does not use sink, leave the stream and finally go, while links that are used, pinned or placed in a workspace stay; it keeps every step visible and reversible until removal, so the owner always knows which state a link is in and why; and it checks every kept link's address weekly, so that a site that has gone is marked dead while its stored copy remains readable.

## Goals

- Every link the owner has not used sinks in the stream by last use, becomes dormant after a fixed period of non-use, is archived after a longer one and removed after a further fixed period, with the owner able to see at any time which state a link is in and why.
- Using a link resets its decay; a link used often enough becomes sticky and never decays; a pinned link and a link in a workspace are never archived by decay.
- The Archive page lists archived links with the date each will be removed, and each can be restored to the top of the stream or deleted.
- Dead links are detected by a weekly liveness check and marked as such in the stream, and a dead link's stored snapshot and reader view stay available.
- Decay and liveness evaluation runs at least once per day for every user; a link's shown state is never more than 24 hours stale.

## Non-goals

- Search on the Archive page (the source PRD's "the same search as the stream"), and the `state:archived`, `state:any` and `is:dead` filters: package 06 (`search_and_browse`) adds the search box to the Archive page.
- Fetching, snapshots, reader view, refresh and the per-host gate: package 02 (`fetch_and_snapshot`); this package sends its checks through package 02's outbound request path and per-host gate.
- The MCP tool `archive_link`: package 08 (`mcp_server`). Decay settings and archive state in the export: package 09 (`export_and_account_deletion`).
- Recovering a removed link: removal is permanent.
- Notifying the owner (email, push) about links that became dormant, archived, removed or dead.
- Checking archived, `pending` or `unreachable` links for liveness.

## Background

Package 01 (`accounts_links_and_stream`) stores links with `state`, `added_at`, `last_used_at`, `use_count` and `pin_position`, records every use in `link_uses` through `recordUse` in `src/worker/links/use.ts`, boosts a re-pasted link in `src/worker/links/store.ts`, already leaves `archived` links out of the stream (`src/worker/links/stream.ts`), and deletes a link with `DELETE /api/v1/links/{id}`. Package 02 (`fetch_and_snapshot`) fetches each link through one outbound request path in `src/worker/fetcher/` that checks every target and redirect for blocked addresses, spaces requests to each host at least 1 second apart through the `HOST_GATE` Durable Object, stores snapshots in R2 (`SNAPSHOTS`) and reader text in D1, deletes those objects with their link, and serves Read and Snapshot even when the origin is gone. Package 04 (`workspaces_and_notes`) stores workspace membership in `workspace_links`. Nothing decays and nothing is checked after the first fetch yet; there is no Cron Trigger, no Archive page and no `dormant` or `archived` link is ever produced. Every component this package names under `src/worker/decay/` and the Archive page are new.

## Requirements

### The stream: decay, sticky, archive

- **Decay**: a link not used for 60 days becomes `dormant`: still in the stream, shown dimmed, with "unused for 2 months". A link not used for 120 days is **archived** automatically: it leaves the stream, keeps its snapshot, and is listed on the Archive page with the date it will be removed. A link archived for a further 180 days (300 days unused in total) is **removed**: deleted permanently with its snapshot. Thresholds are per user settings with these defaults, each between 7 and 3650 days.
- **Use**: using a link resets its decay.
- **Sticky**: a link with at least 5 uses on at least 5 distinct days is sticky: it never becomes dormant or archived by decay; the stream marks it. A pinned link and a link that belongs to at least one workspace are likewise never archived by decay (they can become dormant and show as such). Manual archive and manual delete always work regardless.
- **Archive page**: lists archived links newest-archived first; each can be **restored** (back to `active`, last used = now) or deleted. Removal by decay runs once a day; a link restored before that is kept.
- Decay and liveness evaluation runs at least once per day for every user; a link's shown state is never more than 24 hours stale.

### Liveness

- Every `active`, `dormant` and pinned link is re-checked every 7 days: HEAD then GET on failure, 10-second timeout, at most 5 redirects, never more than 1 request per second per host. A check passes on HTTP 2xx or 3xx (ending in 2xx). A link that fails 3 consecutive weekly checks is marked **dead** with the last status or error, shown in the stream with a strike-through title and "dead since <date>"; its snapshot and reader view remain available. A dead link that passes a later check is cleared automatically. The user can trigger a check for one link on demand (the same 10-minute limit as refresh).
- Archived links are not checked. A dead link follows the normal decay rules; being dead does not itself archive or remove it.
- If the liveness run cannot complete for a user (platform limit, outage) the links keep their previous state and are checked on the next run; nothing is marked dead on the strength of a failed run.

### HTTP API and website

- Archive, restore, the archive list, the on-demand check and the decay settings are authenticated JSON routes under `/api/v1/`, with package 01's error envelope; a request for another user's link gets 404.
- The settings page gains the three decay thresholds.
- End-to-end flows the system must support unbroken:
  1. A link unused for 120 days disappears from the stream and appears on the Archive page with its removal date; the owner restores it; it is back at the top of the stream.
  2. A site goes offline; after three weekly failed checks its card is struck through with "dead since <date>"; "Read" still shows the stored article.

## Design Decisions

1. **Decay is driven solely by last use** (plus the sticky, pin and workspace exemptions), not by a computed score, so the owner can always see why a link is where it is. (Source PRD decision 4.)
2. **Decay thresholds**: dormant at 60 days, archived at 120, removed 180 days after archiving; sticky at 5 uses on 5 distinct days. Owner's decision (source PRD decision 7); every threshold is a per-user setting from 7 to 3650 days.
3. **The dormant threshold must be below the archive threshold**; a setting that breaks this is refused with 400 `invalid_thresholds`. Decided in this run: otherwise a link would skip dormancy and the settings would contradict themselves.
4. **Only an `active` link becomes `dormant`.** A `pending` or `unreachable` link keeps its state while it ages and is archived by decay like any other; a dormant link that is used, re-pasted or restored becomes `active` at once, in the request that boosted it. Decided in this run: `dormant` replaces `active` in the single state column, and an unreachable link's reason is worth more than a dimmed card.
5. **"Distinct days" are UTC calendar days** of the stored use events. Decided in this run: a fixed time zone makes stickiness the same for every reader of the data.
6. **The scheduler runs every hour** (Cron Trigger `0 * * * *`). Each run evaluates decay, removal included, for every user whose last completed evaluation started 20 hours or more ago, and enqueues the liveness checks that are due. Decided in this run: an hourly run keeps every state within 24 hours even when one run fails, and evaluation is set-based SQL per user, so a user of 20,000 links costs a handful of statements.
7. **Liveness checks run on their own Cloudflare Queue, `LIVENESS_QUEUE`.** A link is due when 7 days have passed since its last check (or, never checked, since it was added) and no check of it was enqueued in the last 6 hours; a message that is lost or fails for Alexandria's own reasons is therefore enqueued again by a later run. Decided in this run.
8. **A check's failure is an origin failure only**: a DNS, connection, TLS or timeout error, a blocked redirect, more than 5 redirects, or a final status that is not 2xx. An error of Alexandria's own (the queue consumer failing, the per-host gate unavailable, a platform limit) is a failed run: it changes nothing on the link. Decided in this run, from the source PRD's "nothing is marked dead on the strength of a failed run".
9. **HEAD is retried as GET** when HEAD fails in any way, the GET reading at most the response headers; the GET's outcome is the check's. Decided in this run, from the source PRD's "HEAD then GET on failure".
10. **An on-demand check counts only when it passes.** A pass clears `dead` and the failure count; a failure is shown and stored as the last result but does not add to the consecutive weekly failures, so three quick clicks cannot kill a link. Decided in this run, from the source PRD's "3 consecutive weekly checks".
11. **The on-demand check answers synchronously and is limited to one per link per 10 minutes**, a second answering 429 `checked_recently` with `Retry-After`, as package 02's refresh does. Checking an archived link is refused with 409 `link_archived`. Decided in this run.
12. **Archiving a pinned link unpins it**, closing the gap in the pin positions; workspace memberships are kept. Restoring does not re-pin. Decided in this run: the pinned section is part of the stream, which an archived link leaves.
13. **Restoring is a boost, not a use**: last used becomes now and the use count is unchanged, as for a re-paste in package 01. Restoring a link that is not archived is refused with 409 `not_archived`; archiving an archived link answers 200 and changes nothing. Decided in this run.
14. **Every link carries `decay_note`**, one sentence saying its state and why ("unused for 63 days", "sticky: 7 uses on 6 days, never archived", "pinned: never archived", "in a workspace: never archived", "archived on 2027-03-01, removed on 2027-08-28"). Decided in this run, to meet the goal "able to see at any time which state a link is in and why".
15. **"Unused for N" reads in days below 60 days and in whole months of 30 days from 60 days**, so the default dormant link reads "unused for 2 months". Decided in this run.
16. **Liveness checks go through package 02's outbound request path**, with its blocked-address checks, its `ORIGIN_PROXY_URL` test seam and its `HOST_GATE`, so fetches and checks share one per-host spacing. Decided in this run.

## Dependencies

- Package 01 (`accounts_links_and_stream`): links, `recordUse`, the boost on re-paste, the stream's exclusion of archived links, link deletion, the error envelope, cursors, the OpenAPI document, the Settings page, `LinkCard` and the shared test helpers.
- Package 02 (`fetch_and_snapshot`): the outbound request path, `HOST_GATE`, the snapshot objects deleted with a link, the Read view that works when the origin is gone, and `e2e/fake-origin.ts`.
- Package 04 (`workspaces_and_notes`): workspace membership, which exempts a link from archiving by decay.

## Glossary

- **use**: an open, read or snapshot view of a link, recorded with a timestamp; the unit decay is measured against.
- **boost**: resetting a link's last use to now (what a use, a re-paste or a restore does).
- **decay**: the progression active → dormant → archived → removed, by days since last use.
- **dormant**: an active link unused for longer than the dormant threshold, shown dimmed.
- **archived**: a link out of the stream, retained with its snapshot, scheduled for removal.
- **removed**: deleted permanently with its snapshot by decay.
- **sticky**: a link with at least 5 uses on at least 5 distinct days, which decay no longer makes dormant or archives.
- **dead**: a link whose URL has failed three consecutive weekly liveness checks.
- **liveness check**: a HEAD (then GET) request to a link's URL that passes on a final 2xx status.
- **failed run**: a scheduled evaluation or check that did not complete for Alexandria's own reasons; it changes no link.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Decay thresholds as per-user settings

**Rationale:** How fast a library forgets is the owner's choice, within bounds that keep the rules meaningful.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN a user requests GET /api/v1/settings/decay, THE Alexandria API SHALL return the user's three decay thresholds in days, the defaults being 60 for dormant, 120 for archive and 180 for removal after archiving
   → HTTP 200 with body {dormant_days, archive_days, remove_days}; {60, 120, 180} for a user who never changed them
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts: r = api('GET', '/api/v1/settings/decay', {as: signIn('owner@example.test')}); assert r.status == 200 and r.json == {dormant_days: 60, archive_days: 120, remove_days: 180}
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN a user requests PUT /api/v1/settings/decay with three integers from 7 to 3650 where dormant_days is less than archive_days, THE Alexandria API SHALL store the thresholds, so that every later decay evaluation of that user applies them
   → HTTP 200 with body {dormant_days, archive_days, remove_days} equal to the request
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts: PUT {dormant_days: 7, archive_days: 14, remove_days: 7}; assert 200 and GET returns the same; seed links unused 8 and 15 days and an archived link archived 8 days ago; evaluateDecay(user); assert states dormant, archived, and the old archived link removed; assert another user's thresholds are still the defaults; and the bounds 7 and 3650 are accepted
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF PUT /api/v1/settings/decay carries a threshold that is missing, not an integer, below 7 or above 3650, or a dormant_days that is not less than archive_days, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL refuse the request and keep the stored thresholds
   → HTTP 400 with body {"error": "invalid_threshold", "field": <the threshold's name>, "message": <text>} for a bad value, or {"error": "invalid_thresholds", "field": "dormant_days", "message": "the dormant threshold must be below the archive threshold"}; GET answers the previous values
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, a table over bodies {remove_days absent: invalid_threshold remove_days; dormant_days 6: invalid_threshold dormant_days; archive_days 3651: invalid_threshold archive_days; remove_days 7.5: invalid_threshold remove_days; dormant_days '60': invalid_threshold dormant_days; dormant_days 120 with archive_days 120: invalid_thresholds dormant_days}: assert status 400, error and field; assert GET still returns the previous values
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN the owner opens the decay section of the settings page and saves new thresholds, THE website SHALL show the three thresholds in days with their meaning, send them with PUT /api/v1/settings/decay, and show the API's message next to the field it names when the save is refused
   → the fields show the stored values; Save sends PUT with the three integers; a 400 shows its message beside the named field and keeps the typed values
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/web/pages/Settings.test.tsx with a fake API: renderPage('/settings'); assert fields 'Dormant after (days)' 60, 'Archive after (days)' 120, 'Remove after archiving (days)' 180; change to 30, 90, 30 and Save; assert one PUT with those integers; with the fake API answering 400 invalid_thresholds assert the message beside the dormant field and the typed values kept
   ```

### REQ-2: Dormancy and stickiness

**Rationale:** A link the owner stopped using should fade before it goes, and a link the owner keeps coming back to should never fade.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN the decay evaluation runs for a user and finds an active link that is not sticky and was last used at least dormant_days ago, THE decay evaluation SHALL set the link's state to dormant, whether or not it is pinned or in a workspace
   → the link's state is 'dormant' and it is still listed by GET /api/v1/links in its last-used place
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, a table over (link, days unused, expected state): (active, 59, active); (active, 60, dormant); (active pinned, 61, dormant); (active in a workspace, 200, dormant); (pending, 61, pending); (unreachable, 61, unreachable); (sticky active, 100, active): setNow(t); seed with last_used_at = t - days; evaluateDecay(user); assert the state; assert dormant links are still in GET /api/v1/links
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN a dormant link is boosted by a use (open, read or snapshot view), by being added again or by any other boost, THE Alexandria API SHALL set its state to active in the same request that boosts it
   → the boosting request's response and every later read show state 'active'
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, a table over boosts {GET /api/v1/links/{id}/open, POST /api/v1/links with the same URL, POST /api/v1/links/batch with the same URL}: seed a dormant link; perform the boost; assert GET /api/v1/links/{id}.state == 'active' without running the evaluation
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] THE decay evaluation SHALL for any link, treat it as sticky exactly when its stored uses number at least 5 and fall on at least 5 distinct UTC calendar days, and never make a sticky link dormant or archive it by decay, returning a sticky dormant link to active at the next evaluation
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, a table of (use times, sticky?): (5 uses on 5 days, yes); (10 uses on 4 days, no); (4 uses on 4 days, no); (5 uses at 23:59 and 00:01 UTC across 5 midnights spanning 5 days, yes): seed the uses through recordUse with setNow, then age the link 400 days; evaluateDecay(user); assert sticky in GET /api/v1/links/{id} and the state is active when sticky and archived when not; and a sticky link stored as dormant becomes active after evaluateDecay
   ```

### REQ-3: Archiving and removal by decay

**Rationale:** Links nobody uses must leave the stream and, unless rescued, the library, without ever taking one the owner chose to keep.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN the decay evaluation runs for a user and finds a link that is not archived, was last used at least archive_days ago, and is neither sticky, pinned nor a member of any workspace, THE decay evaluation SHALL archive the link, setting archived_at to the evaluation time, so that it leaves the stream and keeps its snapshot
   → the link's state is 'archived', archived_at equals the evaluation time and removal_at equals archived_at plus remove_days; GET /api/v1/links no longer lists it and GET /api/v1/archive does; its snapshot is still served
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts, a table over (link, days unused, expected): (active, 120, archived); (dormant, 130, archived); (unreachable, 125, archived); (pending, 119, pending); (pinned dormant, 400, dormant); (dormant in a workspace, 400, dormant); (sticky, 400, active); (active with dead_since set, 120, archived); (active with dead_since set, 30, active): setNow(t); evaluateDecay(user); assert state, archived_at and removal_at; assert membership in the stream and the archive list
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN the decay evaluation runs for a user and finds an archived link whose archived_at is at least remove_days before the evaluation time, THE decay evaluation SHALL remove the link permanently, exactly as DELETE /api/v1/links/{id} deletes one, its snapshot objects, reader text, use and fetch events and workspace memberships included
   → GET /api/v1/links/{id} answers 404; no R2 object remains under u/{user_id}/l/{link_id}/; no row of the link remains in any table; an archived link 1 day short of the threshold is still listed by GET /api/v1/archive
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts: seed two archived links with snapshot objects in SNAPSHOTS, archived remove_days and remove_days - 1 days ago; evaluateDecay(user); assert the first answers 404, env.SNAPSHOTS.list({prefix: 'u/' + user + '/l/' + id + '/'}) is empty and no table holds its id; assert the second is still archived with its snapshot
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] THE decay evaluation SHALL for any link and any thresholds, leave after one evaluation exactly the state the decay rules give for its state, days since last use, days since archiving, stickiness, pin and workspace membership, whatever its dead mark
   Check: property
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts: for generated links over state {pending, active, unreachable, dormant, archived}, days unused 0..1000, days archived 0..400, sticky, pinned, member and dead each true or false, and thresholds with 7 <= dormant < archive <= 3650 and remove in 7..3650: seed, evaluateDecay(user) at a fixed time; assert the result equals a reference function of the rule table (removed, archived, dormant, active, or unchanged pending/unreachable); assert running evaluateDecay a second time changes nothing
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF a link is used, restored or added again after the decay evaluation selected it and before the evaluation writes, THEN THE decay evaluation SHALL leave the link as the boost left it, archiving or removing only links whose last use and archive date still meet the thresholds at the moment of the write
   → the boosted link's state is 'active' with the boost's last_used_at; it is listed by GET /api/v1/links
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts: seed a link unused 130 days; run evaluateDecay with a test hook that opens the link through GET /api/v1/links/{id}/open after selection and before the write; assert the link is active, in the stream, and archived_at is null
   ```
1. [REQ-3.5] IF the decay evaluation of one user fails before it completes, THEN THE decay evaluation SHALL leave every link of that user exactly as it was before the evaluation, carry on with the other users, and evaluate the failing user again at the next hourly run
   → no link of the failing user changed; the other users' due links are evaluated in the same run; the failing user's last completed evaluation time is unchanged, so the next run selects the user again
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts: users A and B each with a link unused 130 days; make A's evaluation throw after its selection through a test hook; runScheduled(t); assert A's link unchanged and B's archived; remove the hook; runScheduled(t + 1 hour); assert A's link archived
   ```
1. [REQ-3.6] WHEN the hourly scheduled run starts, THE scheduler SHALL evaluate decay, removal included, for every user whose last completed evaluation started 20 hours or more ago or who was never evaluated, and for no other user
   → after the run, those users' last completed evaluation time equals the run's start time; the others' is unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts: users evaluated 19 h ago, 20 h ago and never, each with a link unused 130 days; runScheduled(t) through the Worker's scheduled handler; assert the 19 h user's link is unchanged and the other two are archived; assert their last evaluation times == t
   ```

### REQ-4: Why a link is in its state

   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN the website shows a card for a dormant or sticky link, THE website SHALL show a dormant link's card dimmed with its 'unused for …' text, and mark a sticky link's card as sticky

### REQ-5: Manual archive, the archive list and restore

**Rationale:** The owner can always put a link away or bring one back, whatever decay would do.

[REQ-5.1] WHEN a user requests POST /api/v1/links/{id}/archive for one of their links, THE Alexandria API SHALL archive the link whatever its stickiness, pin or workspace membership, setting archived_at to now, unpinning it and closing the gap in the pin positions, and keeping its workspace memberships; an already archived link is left unchanged

1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN a user requests POST /api/v1/links/{id}/restore for one of their archived links, THE Alexandria API SHALL make the link active with last used set to now and no archive date, leaving its use count unchanged, so that it is at the top of the stream after the pinned links

### REQ-6: Scheduling weekly liveness checks

**Rationale:** Every kept link is checked weekly, and nothing else is checked at all.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN the hourly scheduled run starts, THE scheduler SHALL enqueue one liveness check on LIVENESS_QUEUE for every link that is not archived, is active or dormant or pinned, was last checked 7 days ago or more (or, never checked, was added 7 days ago or more), and had no check enqueued in the last 6 hours, recording the enqueue time
   → one queue message {user_id, link_id} per due link; the link's check_enqueued_at equals the run's time; no message for any other link
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/liveness.test.ts, a table over (link, enqueued?): (active, checked 7 days ago, yes); (dormant, checked 8 days ago, yes); (pinned unreachable, checked 10 days ago, yes); (active, checked 6 days ago, no); (active never checked, added 7 days ago, yes); (active never checked, added 2 days ago, no); (archived, checked 30 days ago, no); (pending, added 30 days ago, no); (unreachable unpinned, no); (active due but enqueued 5 hours ago, no); (active due, enqueued 7 hours ago, yes): runScheduled(t) with a recording LIVENESS_QUEUE; assert the messages
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] IF a liveness message names a link that has since been deleted or archived, or that is no longer due, THEN THE liveness check SHALL drop the message without sending any request and without changing any row
   → the message is acknowledged; the fake origin of src/worker/test/origin.ts logs no request; the link's fields are unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/liveness.test.ts, a table over {deleted link, archived link, link checked 1 hour ago}: deliver the message to the queue handler; assert it is acked, no outbound request was made and no row changed
   ```

### REQ-7: Performing a liveness check and marking dead links

**Rationale:** Only the origin's own answer may count against a link, and only three weeks of silence make it dead.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN a liveness check of a link is performed, THE liveness check SHALL send a HEAD request to the link's URL through package 02's outbound request path and per-host gate, with a 10-second timeout and at most 5 redirects, and when the HEAD fails in any way send a GET the same way, reading no more than its headers; the check passes when the last request's final status is 2xx
   → the outcome is {passed: boolean, result: 'HTTP <status>' | 'timed out' | 'could not connect' | 'blocked address' | 'too many redirects'}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/liveness.test.ts with the fake origin of src/worker/test/origin.ts, a table of (origin behaviour, requests sent, outcome): (HEAD 200, [HEAD], passed 'HTTP 200'); (HEAD 301 to a 200, [HEAD, HEAD], passed 'HTTP 200'); (HEAD 405 then GET 200, [HEAD, GET], passed 'HTTP 200'); (HEAD 404 then GET 404, [HEAD, GET], failed 'HTTP 404'); (no answer for 10 s on both, [HEAD, GET], failed 'timed out'); (connection refused, [HEAD, GET], failed 'could not connect'); (6 redirects, failed 'too many redirects'); (redirect to http://10.0.0.1, failed 'blocked address'): checkLink(link); assert the requests, each via HOST_GATE, and the outcome
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] WHEN a scheduled liveness check passes, THE liveness check SHALL set the link's consecutive failure count to 0, clear its dead mark, and store the check time and result
   → liveness_failures 0, dead_since null, last_checked_at the check time, last_check_result 'HTTP 200'
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/liveness.test.ts: a link with liveness_failures 3 and dead_since set; the fake origin answers HEAD 200; deliver its message; assert liveness_failures 0, dead_since null, last_checked_at == now, last_check_result 'HTTP 200'
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] WHEN a scheduled liveness check fails because of the origin, THE liveness check SHALL add one to the link's consecutive failure count, store the check time and result, and on the third consecutive failure set dead_since to the check time, keeping an earlier dead_since of a link already dead
   → after failures 1 and 2 dead_since is null; after failure 3 dead_since equals the third check's time; later failures leave dead_since unchanged; state, snapshot and decay fields are unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/liveness.test.ts: the fake origin refuses connections; deliver the link's message at t, t + 7 d, t + 14 d, t + 21 d; assert liveness_failures 1, 2, 3, 4; dead_since null, null, t + 14 d, t + 14 d; last_check_result 'could not connect'; state and last_used_at unchanged; and a pass between the second and third failure resets the count so the next failure is 1
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] IF a liveness check cannot complete for Alexandria's own reasons: the queue handler throws, the per-host gate is unavailable or a platform limit stops it, THEN THE liveness check SHALL change nothing on the link and leave it to be checked again by a later run
   → liveness_failures, dead_since, last_checked_at and last_check_result are unchanged; the message is retried by the queue, and once the 6-hour window passes a later scheduled run enqueues the link again
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/liveness.test.ts, a table over {HOST_GATE made unavailable through a test hook, the check's store write throws}: a link with liveness_failures 2; deliver its message; assert the message is retried (not acked) and the link's liveness fields unchanged; runScheduled(t + 7 h); assert a new message for it
   ```
1. [REQ-7.5] THE liveness check SHALL for any set of due links on one host, send their liveness requests at least 1 second apart, together with the fetches package 02 sends to that host
   Check: integration
   - setup: the real HOST_GATE Durable Object in the Workers test runtime
   - setup: five due links on host a.example and one fetch of a.example queued by package 02
   ```
   in src/worker/decay/liveness.test.ts: deliver the five liveness messages and the fetch message together; record the time each outbound request to a.example arrives at the fake origin of src/worker/test/origin.ts; assert consecutive times differ by at least 1000 ms
   ```

[REQ-8.1] WHEN a user requests POST /api/v1/links/{id}/check for one of their links that is not archived and was not checked on demand in the last 10 minutes, THE Alexandria API SHALL perform a liveness check now and answer with its outcome; a pass clears the dead mark and the failure count, and a failure stores the check time and result without adding to the consecutive weekly failures

   ```

   → the detail page shows 'Reachable (HTTP 200), checked just now' or 'Not reachable (could not connect), checked just now'; a 429 shows 'already checked recently'

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A link unused for 120 days is archived and the owner restores it

1. **scheduler** runs the hourly evaluation for the owner, whose link 'https://example.org/old' was last used 121 days ago
2. **scheduler** archives the link with today's date and a removal date 180 days later
3. **owner** opens the stream and no longer finds the link
4. **owner** opens the Archive page
5. **Alexandria API** answers GET /api/v1/archive with the link and its removal date
6. **website** shows the link with 'removed on <date>' and a Restore action
7. **owner** chooses Restore
8. **Alexandria API** makes the link active with last used now
9. **website** shows the link at the top of the stream

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** scheduler, Alexandria API, website, D1 database

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev --test-scheduled with local D1, the owner signed in through e2e/fake-google.ts
- one link added through the API whose last_used_at is then set 121 days back with wrangler d1 execute --local

**End state:**

- after the scheduled run the link's state was 'archived' with removal_at 180 days after archived_at, and the stream did not list it
- after Restore the link's state is 'active', archived_at is null and last_used_at is the restore time
- the stream shows the link first and the Archive page is empty

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/decay.spec.ts: add the link; set last_used_at back with wrangler d1 execute; request /__scheduled?cron=0+*+*+*+*; on / expect no card for the link; on /archive expect its row with 'removed on' the date; click Restore; on / expect it first; on /archive expect no rows
```

### PATH-2: A site goes offline, is marked dead after three weekly checks, and its copy is still readable

1. **owner** adds a link to an article page served by the fake origin site
2. **fetch worker** fetches the article and stores its snapshot and reader view
3. **scheduler** enqueues the link's weekly liveness check in three runs a week apart, while the origin refuses connections
4. **Alexandria API** performs each check through the per-host gate, counts three consecutive failures and sets dead since to the third check's date
5. **owner** sees the card's title struck through with 'dead since <date>'
6. **owner** chooses Read on the card
7. **Alexandria API** serves the stored reader view without contacting the origin
8. **website** shows the stored article

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** scheduler, liveness queue consumer, HOST_GATE, fetch worker, Alexandria API, website, D1 database, R2 snapshots

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev --test-scheduled with local D1, R2 and Queues, ORIGIN_PROXY_URL pointing at e2e/fake-origin.ts, the owner signed in through e2e/fake-google.ts
- e2e/fake-origin.ts serves the article, then is switched to refuse connections for its host

**End state:**

- the link's liveness_failures is 3 and dead_since is set
- the stream card's title is struck through and reads 'dead since <date>'
- the Read view shows the stored article's heading and text while the origin still refuses connections

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/liveness.spec.ts: add the fake origin's article URL; wait for the card to become active; switch the fake origin offline; three times: set last_checked_at and check_enqueued_at 7 days back with wrangler d1 execute, request /__scheduled and wait until last_checked_at changes; reload /; expect the struck title and 'dead since'; click Read; expect the article heading
```
